videos.script: A router's job is to deliver packets. It does that job very well, to anybody. {{open}} In this course's lab, a stranger on the internet opens the company's database port. Nothing is broken to do it. Nothing on the path was asked whether it should. {{map}} A firewall is where that question gets asked. It is a list of questions about each packet, and a verdict for each answer. {{rules}} This lesson writes the same policy twice. First without memory, where every packet is judged alone. You will watch the replies vanish, and then watch the rule that brings them back let in something nobody meant to allow. {{hole}} Then with memory: connection tracking, the table of conversations a stateful firewall keeps. You will read that table, read the counters, and see what keeping it costs. {{table}}
